text.content:
Every contest runs the same way, whether it is a duel, an argument, or a crisis of belief (PHB 1.4.0, 6.4.0).

  1. Declare the Instrument and the Technique: one of the Instrument's built-in Techniques, or one the character has learned.
  2. Name the Attribute it harms. Describe the action; the GM judges whether it fits.
  3. Pick any of the three Skills the Instrument's Primary Attribute allows.
  4. Pay the Action, or the Quick Action for a Quick-tagged Technique or a Light built-in after a Light Action. A Stress Technique through a Heavy Instrument takes both. A signature takes the Action.
  5. Roll the Skill. The target Opposes with any Skill built on the Attribute under attack, or, against a Technique that deals no Stress, with any Skill built on the Attribute its Condition names. A kit roll that only applies a Condition says which.
  6. If the Oppose beats the roll, the Technique fails. Otherwise it lands, a tie landing at a margin of 0.

There is no separate damage roll. The margin the Technique won by becomes its Stress.

A character has four Attributes: Might and Finesse (physical), Wit and Presence (mental). Each is a pool of dice. Every Attribute starts at 2d4; an Origin and a Background add to them (PHB 2.5.0).

Potential is the most that pool can roll. It is also how much Stress the Attribute holds before it is Incapacitated.

Six Skills each pair two Attributes. To roll one, roll both pools and add that Skill's Training.

SkillAttributesRepresents
ProwessMight + FinesseAthletics, martial arts, power
DisciplineMight + WitControl, resilience, consistency
AssertivenessMight + PresenceIntimidation, command, inspiration, rallying
AcuityFinesse + WitPerception, awareness, foresight
GuileFinesse + PresenceManeuvering, deception, performance, misdirection
ResonanceWit + PresenceInsight, persuasion, connection, encouragement

Training costs 8 XP, plus 2 for each point the Skill already has. It can't pass the number of dice in the Skill's two pools.

A creature that isn't pushing back has a Passive Skill for each Skill: half the Skill's Potential, rounded down. It stands in as the Difficulty.

An Instrument has one Range, one Primary Attribute, and a weight class. One that can harm has one Instrument Type, and many have Properties (PHB 4.1.1). The Primary Attribute sets which three Skills can roll it. No Type or Property adds Stress.

TypeHarms
MeleeMight or Finesse
RangedMight or Finesse
ArcaneMight or Finesse through Kinetic, Wit or Presence through Incorporeal
SonicWit or Presence. Its Conditions reach each hearer its user chooses within its Range. Its Stress lands on one target.
PropertyEffect
GrapplingIt can hold a creature
GuardingIt guards its user or an ally within its Range
Kinetic, IncorporealWhat an Arcane Instrument harms. With both, the user picks one for each Technique.
ThrownA Melee Instrument with it is thrown out to Range 4
Drawn / FiredReload with the Quick Action / the Action
ImmobileFixed in place
ToolsIts rolls are Trades

A Melee, Ranged, or Sonic Instrument has two built-in Techniques (PHB 4.1.3). Most pair a Stress Technique with its family's signature. A signature costs the Action at any weight. A signature priced over 11 XP costs 1 Strain for each full 8 XP over. The third Skill backs Voice: while the Instrument is ready, Voice's Technique on that Skill gets +2 against a target within its Range. An Arcane Instrument has no built-ins.

Every character has three innate Instruments, always ready. Body is Might Primary, Light, Melee, Grappling, Range 1: Strike and Grapple, and it backs Threaten. Voice is Presence Primary, Light, Sonic, Range 8: Threaten, Deceive, and Persuade, each dealing Stress or applying one of two Conditions. Mind is Wit Primary, Light, Range 2: Deduce, Analyze, Intuit.

Light, Medium, and Heavy are weight classes. They set an Instrument's base price (15p, 30p, 45p) and its carried weight (2, 4, 8 lbs). A Heavy Instrument takes both hands. A Stress Technique through it costs the Action and the Quick Action, and its margin doubles before the cap. After an Action through a Light Instrument, the Quick Action can use a Light Instrument's built-in Technique other than a signature.

When a Stress Technique lands (PHB 6.7.0):

  1. Take the margin, capped at a share of the Instrument's Primary Potential by its weight: half for Light, all for Medium, and all for Heavy after doubling. Only the margin is capped.
  2. Add the Technique's own Effects, such as +1 Stress.
  3. Subtract the target's Resistance, less any Pierce, to a minimum of 0.

Resistance comes in two kinds. Physical covers Might and Finesse. Mental covers Wit and Presence.

Guard (PHB 6.5.1) costs the Quick Action, through a ready Guarding Instrument. It works on your turn, or when a Technique targets you or an ally within its Range, before the Oppose. For 1 round, the guarded character gets +2 to Oppose, and the Instrument's +N on top. It covers the Attributes the Instrument harms.

An Attribute is Incapacitated when its Stress reaches its Potential. It contributes no dice. Incapacitation lifts once healing brings its Stress down to half its Potential or less, rounded down. Stress past a full bar overflows onto another Attribute, the defender's choice, and the receiving Attribute's Resistance doesn't reduce it.

Destroyed is all four Attributes Incapacitated at once. It is permanent, and a choice a side makes.

Each round a character gets one Action and one Quick Action. The Quick Action is spent on your turn or held to use reactively, one use either way. Moving up to 20 feet is free; another 20 costs the Quick Action. Initiative is an Acuity roll.

A learned Technique carries Strain: floor((XP - 24) / 8) Stress to its own user, on the Instrument's Primary Attribute, whether it lands or not, ignoring Resistance. A Technique under 32 XP carries none. A built-in Technique carries only the Strain it states.

Four axes describe how a character responds in the moment: Faith (Trusting or Mistrusting), Order (Methodical or Intuitive), Individualism (Individual or Communal), and Levity (Light or Grave). Each leans toward one end or stays Neutral (PHB 3.1.0).

Once per scene a player may invoke a Habit their character holds. If the table agrees the Habit drives what the character is doing, they earn a Foil Token. A character holds at most four.

A Foil Token is spent at will: halve the Stress from one source, rounded down, or reroll any one die right after rolling a Skill. The new result stands.

A conflict ends when one side stops contesting it. Flee: Disengage and move away; each chaser rolls Prowess against the fleer every round, and the winner moves up to Range 2. Yield: stop fighting and accept terms. Destroy: keep going until every Attribute is Incapacitated. Terms: press for an end with social Conditions.

Rest removes 1d4 Stress every 2 hours from one Attribute of the character's choice. It starts by eating one ration, which covers up to 8 hours of recovery; without one, the time passes but heals nothing.

Toil is effort sustained over stretches of about 8 hours, such as travel or labor. Each stretch is one roll for the party: Prowess for heavy work or very difficult terrain, Acuity to find the way or to search, Discipline otherwise. A stretch costs 1 Strain on every Attribute, 2 on a failure. Each 2 hours past 8 without a rest adds 1 more. Strain ignores Resistance, and no one can Toil while it would take an Attribute past its Potential. A stretch of travel is a leg.

Gathering (PHB 5.3.3) takes 2 hours and a Trade roll through a gathering Tool: food yields 1 ration plus 1 per 4 points of margin, and a Herbalist's Satchel or Craft Tool finds a batch of material at a Tier the region holds, plus 1 per 8 points of margin.

Mass: past 4x Might Potential in pounds, every roll takes -1 per extra multiple, and each stretch of Toil adds that much Strain.
